carousels.name: The side doors to p*rn: Reddit, games, anime

slides.title: But p*rn is still getting in [[through the side doors.]]
slides.sub: The places nobody thinks to block.

slides.title: [[Reddit]] and forums
slides.body: NSFW subreddits and "just browsing" threads are p*rn by another name. If you're trying to quit p*rn, these count.

slides.title: Games and [[anime]] art
slides.body: Fan art, character edits, "harmless" game communities. Many people say this is where their p*rn relapses quietly started.

slides.title: Search [[images]]
slides.body: One innocent search, then image results, then "related" — and you're back on p*rn. Turn on SafeSearch everywhere.

slides.title: Close the [[side doors]]
items: Block NSFW communities along with p*rn sites.
Turn on SafeSearch on every browser.
Mute art accounts that drift into p*rn.
Be honest about where your relapses start.

slides.title: "Free" p*rn [[isn't free anymore.]]
slides.sub: How p*rn addiction quietly drains your wallet.

slides.title: [[Subscriptions]]
slides.body: Paid p*rn sites. Creator subscriptions. Tips. Small amounts that feel like nothing — until you add them up.

slides.title: The [[escalation]]
slides.body: Free p*rn stops being enough, so you pay for more. Many people say spending on p*rn was the moment they realized it was a problem.

slides.title: The [[hidden]] cost
slides.body: Missed work, lost focus, late nights. P*rn addiction costs more than money — it costs your best hours.

slides.title: Take it [[back]]
items: Check your statements for every p*rn charge.
Cancel all p*rn subscriptions today.
Remove saved cards from your browser.
Put that money toward a goal you care about.

slides.title: You open p*rn every time [[a task feels hard.]]
slides.sub: P*rn isn't just a habit. It's your escape from discomfort.

slides.title: The [[hard-task]] trigger
slides.body: Big assignment, tough email, boring work. Your brain looks for an exit — and p*rn is the fastest one it knows.

slides.title: Procrastination [[+]] p*rn
slides.body: One feeds the other: avoid the task, watch p*rn, feel guilty, avoid the task even harder. Hours vanish.

slides.title: Make the task [[smaller]]
slides.body: The urge to escape is strongest when a task feels huge. Shrink it: "just 10 minutes" beats "finish everything."

slides.title: Next time a task feels [[hard]]
items: Notice the p*rn urge for what it is: avoidance.
Start for 10 minutes — just 10.
Work away from your bed and private spaces.
Keep the p*rn blocker on during work hours.

carousels.name: 5 questions to ask before you open p*rn

slides.title: 5 questions to ask yourself [[before you open p*rn.]]
slides.sub: 30 seconds that can change the whole night.

slides.title: Questions [[1–2]]
items: What am I actually feeling right now? Bored, stressed, lonely, tired?
Will p*rn fix that — or just delay it?

slides.title: Questions [[3–4]]
items: How did I feel the last time I watched p*rn?
What would future me want me to do right now?

slides.title: What can I do for [[10 minutes]] instead?
slides.body: Walk. Shower. Call someone. Do 20 push-ups. Most p*rn urges fade if you give them 10 minutes.

slides.title: Pause [[beats]] willpower.
slides.body: You don't need to win a fight with the urge. You just need to pause long enough to ask. The pause is where you take control back from p*rn.

carousels.name: Incognito mode is a red flag

slides.title: Deleting your p*rn history [[doesn't delete the addiction.]]
slides.sub: Why the hiding rituals are part of the problem.

slides.title: The [[hiding]] ritual
slides.body: Incognito mode. Clearing history. Hidden folders. Second accounts. If you hide your p*rn use this carefully, part of you already knows.

slides.title: Secrecy [[fuels]] it
slides.body: Hiding p*rn feels like protection. It isn't. Secrecy keeps shame high — and shame is one of p*rn addiction's favorite fuels.

slides.title: Openness [[weakens]] it
slides.body: You don't have to tell everyone. But telling one person changes things. Many people say that breaking the secret broke p*rn's grip.

slides.title: Step out of the [[shadows]]
items: Notice your hiding rituals — name them.
Stop clearing history as a reset button.
Tell one trusted person about your p*rn use.
Use accountability instead of secrecy.
slides.note: What's your hiding ritual? Comment it — no judgment here 👇
